SCAN / OPTIMIZE / RECONSTRUCT

From scan to web preview

Following drone photogrammetry, the scanned model was optimized for web viewing. Floating fragments were removed and selected buildings reconstructed using aerial photographs and scan references.

Model optimization

The early campus scan contained approximately 69.64 million triangles. A pre-optimized campus mesh was further reduced from 2,978,362 to 1,009,488 triangles for web viewing; this reduction excludes the base, water and rebuilt buildings.

Viewer & scene integration

The Three.js viewer combines the scanned campus with replacement geometry, camera views and reversible comparisons. The overview shows the library and gymnasium reconstruction stage; the case study below focuses on the library.

LIBRARY / CASE STUDY

Photograph, scan & reconstruction

The aerial photograph is an approximate viewpoint match. The scanned and rebuilt model views use the same camera.

Reference & geometry

The glazed facade, diagonal supports, rear wall and main roof elements were rebuilt using aerial photographs and the scanned model as references.

Local replacement

The rebuilt upper building replaces the scanned geometry. Surrounding terrain, terraces and the building base remain from the scan.

Reconstruction scope

This is an exterior visual reconstruction. Dimensions and details are approximate, and small elements remain simplified.
